key_insight: The paper argues that mega-scale robot RL is often limited less by model capacity and more by the quality of data exploration. A more balanced mix of resets and experience can reduce the need for hand-engineered rewards and demos while improving learning coverage across tasks.
problem_solved: It addresses the exploration bottleneck in sim-to-real reinforcement learning for robot control, where agents fail to discover useful behaviors without expensive task-specific priors like shaped rewards, demonstrations, or manual curriculum design.
method: Use diverse simulator resets to expose the agent to a broader range of initial states and scenarios.
Scale RL with massive parallel simulation to collect large volumes of experience efficiently.
Balance the training data distribution to improve exploration and reduce reliance on engineering-heavy supervision.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more scalable and less labor-intensive path to training general-purpose robot policies. It can simplify pipeline design, reduce reward engineering, and improve transfer from simulation to real robots.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing sim-to-real RL with diverse resets and parallel rollout collection
Before/after comparison of exploration coverage with sparse vs balanced reset distributions
Icon set for robot locomotion, manipulation, and simulation scale
Chart illustrating reduced dependence on rewards/demonstrations versus improved task success
paper_title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
paper_authors: Octi Zhang, Mateo Guaman Castro, Patrick Yin, Ignacio Dagnino, Abhishek Gupta
